title: The value-free four-place knots
claim: The complement-invariant (value-free) four-place knot relations, unions of antipodal pairs of {0,1}^4 whose three-place projections are full, are exactly 30, in four classes under flips and permutations: parity (8 states, 2 relations), not-exactly-two (10 states, 8), twelve (12 states, 12) and not-all-equal (14 states, 8). A complement-invariant law can never pin a value, since every piece's accepted relation is complement-invariant. By Schaefer's theorem only parity is tractable with unbounded occurrences. On plain systems only the eight relations excluding both constants can fail (odd parity, three of not-exactly-two, three of twelve, not-all-equal). Census over every 4-regular 4-uniform system with n <= 7 and every signing: not-all-equal never fails; parity and not-exactly-two fail on every such system; twelve fails on every system with n <= 6 and on 11 of the 14 with n = 7.
failure_conditions: A fifth class of value-free four-place knots, or a class count other than 2, 8, 12, 8.
A piece of a complement-invariant law whose accepted relation is not complement-invariant.
A non-affine class closed under one of Schaefer's tractable polymorphisms.
A 4-regular 4-uniform system with n <= 7 missing from the enumeration.
foundation_claim_scope: A structural classification of value-free four-place relations and a finite census; no counting claim.
